In January 2018, debut author Josh Farkas visited Medium.com to discuss his book Quitting, which he writes serves as a cautionary tale for those considering a career quit vehicle to found an online company.
According to Farkas, he and his team started incubating their business, The Art of Quitting, after becoming fed up with their previous nine to five job in August three years earlier.
They had a straightforward idea for a business intended to assist others in learning how to quit their jobs. To establish the business, they printed some flyers and distributed them in the neighborhood where they were located to advertise their newly formed company.
At the beginning, they faced their first challenge with their business: getting their name approved.
Next to potential market saturation with The Art of Quitting, Farkas would not recommend or encourage using your name to start any business for several reasons.
Establishing a recognizable name or successful business is not an easy task. Not to mention that coming up with a unique name to go forward is even more challenging.
Using Farkas’ experience, name conflicts can arise years before a business is ultimately determined.
In reality, The Art of Quitting, not one of the greatest titles, has undergone several iterations. Farkas stated that the original business concept was named Art of Quitting, but they encountered issues with trademarks.
They pivoted once more in response to a cease and desist letter from a website called Dead Wild Flowers, which already used a similar tile. Instead of facing the issue of possibly receiving cease and desist letters later, they chose to find an alternative name.
In the meantime, they also used software like Verified Domains and Domainr to experiment with other names. This paid off after a discussion with a fellow entrepreneur suggested trying to find names by looking within the current company’s acronyms.
Losing the “quitting,” Farkas said he immediately identified with their current company name
